definitions.ISSUE-01: Whether a killing during forcible confinement is first degree murder absent planning and deliberation (constructive classification under s 231(5)).
definitions.PROP-01: Irrespective of planning and deliberation, murder is first degree when the death is caused while committing or attempting an offence under s 279 (kidnapping and forcible confinement).
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: Section 231(5)(e) is the governing route to first degree murder on these facts and s 231 must rank first.
definitions.CLAIM-01: The terrorism provisions (s 83.01 definitions) govern the classification of this killing.
definitions.CLAIM-02: The Occupiers' Liability Act or the Food and Drug Regulations bear on the murder-classification question.
definitions.CLAIM-03: R. v. Latimer or R. v. Oakes states the governing test for classifying murder committed during forcible confinement.
